summary: Completed backend API regression and browser E2E coverage for public site, owner auth, menu/category CRUD, availability, uploads, gallery, logout, and mobile navigation. Core CRUD and UI flows pass; auth hardening has two findings.

critical.issue: No brute-force lockout after five consecutive failed logins; the sixth failed attempt still returns 401 instead of 423/429.

minor.issue: OPTIONS with Origin https://story-cafe-admin.preview.emergentagent.com returns 400 Disallowed CORS origin and no allow-origin header, despite FRONTEND_URL being configured; same-origin browser flow is unaffected.

action_items: Implement and persist per-account/IP login throttling or lockout after five failed attempts, with a clear 423/429 response.
Fix runtime CORS origin loading so the configured frontend origin passes credentialed preflight requests.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py login has no failed-attempt tracking, rate limit, or lockout path.
CORS origins rely on FRONTEND_URL at import time; verify supervisor runtime environment/.env loading because the public configured origin is rejected by preflight.
seed_data_creation: Created temporary TEST_Category/TEST_Product records through API and UI, then deleted them; public products are empty and only the eight seeded categories remain.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Public home/logo/gallery/empty menu, login/session cookie, unauthenticated mutation rejection, category constraint, product create/edit/toggle/delete, public menu sync, upload, logout, desktop and mobile navigation were exercised. Re-run auth lockout and CORS preflight after fixes.
rca of the issue: Brute-force failure is directly caused by /api/auth/login only querying the user and verifying bcrypt; it has no attempt counter or lockout state. CORS failure is reproducible with an OPTIONS request carrying the configured public Origin; Starlette returns Disallowed CORS origin, indicating the runtime allowed-origin list does not contain that value even though backend/.env declares FRONTEND_URL.
